questions.q: What is the passage mainly about?
options: Carnegie's steel empire and its rivalry with Standard Oil
The rise of kerosene and gasoline as household fuels
Rockefeller's oil empire and his later philanthropy
The Baptist church's role in building Cleveland's industry
questions.explain: It covers Standard Oil, its breakup, and Rockefeller's philanthropy.

questions.q: How many entities was Standard Oil broken into in 1911?
questions.explain: The Supreme Court ordered it dismantled into 34 separate entities.

questions.q: On what date did Rockefeller become the first billionaire?
questions.explain: He became the country's first billionaire on 28 September 1916.

questions.q: What share of the nation's oil production did Standard Oil control by 1900?
questions.explain: By 1900 Standard Oil controlled about 90% of national oil production.

questions.q: What does the passage suggest about Rockefeller's view of business?
options: Large trusts should be broken up for the public good
Competition among oil firms keeps business healthy
Large business growth reflects survival of the fittest
Charity work should be left to churches, not business
questions.explain: He was quoted as saying growth of a large business is merely survival of the fittest.
